overall_safety_summary: The cooking area has two main safety concerns: flammable plastic packaging is placed too close to the gas stove, and a frying pan handle is protruding outwards, creating a risk of accidental bumps.

hazards.description: Flammable plastic food packaging is positioned directly adjacent to the active gas stovetop.
hazards.explanation: The heat or open flame from the burners could melt the plastic or ignite the packaging, presenting a fire risk.
hazards.older_adult_relevance: Older adults with reduced sensory awareness or slower reaction times may not notice melting plastic or a small fire immediately.
hazards.recommended_action: Move all plastic bags and food packaging away from the immediate vicinity of the stove.

hazards.description: The handle of the frying pan is turned outwards to the left, protruding over the edge of the stove.
hazards.explanation: A protruding handle can easily be bumped, leading to the hot pan tipping over and causing burns or spills.
hazards.older_adult_relevance: Older adults with balance or mobility impairments are more susceptible to accidentally knocking into protruding handles.
hazards.recommended_action: Rotate the frying pan handle inward so it is safely positioned over the countertop or stovetop surface.

uncertainties: The exact temperature or flame level of the active burner is not clearly visible.
